newsitem.title: GERMANY: German prosecutor renews accusations against Iran.
newsitem.headline: German prosecutor renews accusations against Iran.

text.p: A German prosecutor on Thursday renewed accusations of "state terrorism" against Iran over a 1992 Berlin murder of Kurdish dissidents, and vowed he would not be intimidated by threats from Tehran.
State prosecutor Bruno Jost also accused Iran of trying to discredit a key witness in the trial with a mix of "half-truths, slanders, lies and false accusations".
"A background of state terrorism has been clearly proved," he said.

Jost was summing up in the murder trial of an Iranian and four Lebanese, accused of involvement in the gunning down of three Kurdish-Iranian opposition leaders and their translator in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant.
Iran denies any role in the attack.
Similar remarks by Jost in a previous summing-up, before the court decided to hear evidence from more witnesses, provoked outrage in Iran last November.
Protesters marched on the German embassy, called for Jost's death and threw eggs and tomatoes at the compound.

"We won't let anyone silence us," Jost told the court on Friday. He also poured scorn on Iranian accusations that his original remarks had crossed an invisible line, offending the Islamic faith and its followers.
"If anyone has overstepped a mark here, then it is those who ordered, planned and carried out the Mykonos attack," he said.
Tehran last year denounced a key prosecution witness, Abolhassem Mesbahi, who says he was an Iranian secret agent.
Iran said he was a Western spy wanted at home on criminal charges, including embezzlement and cheque fraud and was also a wife-beater.
"Iranian government agencies have once again tried to exert massive influence on this trial," Jost said, describing Mesbahi as an "important, good and credible witness".
"Iran's attempt to discredit the witness has proved to be a sorry concoction, a hotchpotch of half-truths, slanders, lies and false accusations," the prosecutor said.
Prosecutors have issued an arrest warrant for Tehran's Intelligence Minister Ali Fallahiyan in connection with the assassinations -- a move which also provoked fury in Iran.

Jost made his statement on the 239th day of the marathon trial, which may finally be drawing to a conclusion. The presiding judge said it was possible a verdict could be announced between March 13 and 21.
